- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 3–5 days of a new trend; adjust forecast upward by 2–4% for early trend entries.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage rallies; add 1–3% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 3+ days, model underperforms; apply upward bias to counteract mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model is prone to oscillation; smooth forecast by averaging 2–3 prior values to reduce noise.
